requirements.requirement: Nginx backends on node1, node2, and node3 serve their respective node identifiers from / on port 5660.
requirements.summary: Direct checks showed all three Nginx services active and enabled, listening on port 5660, and returning the correct identifiers. Final checks after all restarts again returned node1, node2, and node3 from their respective endpoints.

requirements.requirement: HAProxy on node4 serves HTTP on port 80 and distributes requests across healthy backends.
requirements.summary: HAProxy was active and enabled with a port 80 listener. Repeated requests returned node1, node2, and node3 in round-robin order both before disruption and after all node restarts.

requirements.requirement: The HTTP service remains available when any one backend fails and the recovered backend rejoins service.
requirements.summary: A healthy three-backend baseline was observed, node2 was then stopped and confirmed inactive and unreachable, and ten consecutive HAProxy requests succeeded through node1 and node3. After node2 was restored, it returned valid content and rejoined the three-node rotation.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied with direct behavioral evidence. The three Nginx backends return their identifiers, HAProxy serves and distributes traffic on port 80, and a bounded backend outage demonstrated continued availability and successful recovery. The provider-wide restart protocol was also completed coherently on all four nodes.
limitations: The bounded failure test directly disrupted node2 only; node1 and node3 failure handling is supported by the symmetric HAProxy health-check configuration and observed node2 behavior but was not separately disrupted.

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutations were identified. Package installation and service configuration directly established the requested service; the node2 stop/start was a bounded availability test and was fully restored; and the four reboots fulfilled the mandatory restart-evidence protocol. Post-executor snapshots show no failed services, healthy package state, only the required listeners, and no apparent abandoned temporary artifacts. Every node had a healthy pre-restart state, restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, and recovered service/content or load-balancer state; the fixed lifecycle boot identities independently agree with those transitions.
